name: Porro-prism binoculars
definition: twin-barrel binoculars with Porro prisms, giving an offset, Z-shaped body.

name: Giant binoculars
definition: binoculars of 70 to 150 mm aperture, used on a tripod.

name: Opera glasses
definition: small Galilean-design binoculars for the theatre and opera.

name: Monocular
definition: single-tube handheld viewing instrument, not a telescope on a mount.

name: Night-vision viewer
definition: Viewer that boosts available light to show a scene in the dark.

name: Thermal-imaging viewer
definition: Viewer that shows a scene by the heat it gives off.

name: Roof-prism binoculars
definition: twin-barrel binoculars with roof prisms, giving a straight, slim body.

name: Refractor telescope
definition: telescope that gathers light with a lens objective.

name: Newtonian telescope
definition: Telescope that gathers light with a primary mirror and a flat secondary mirror at the side of the tube; the Dobsonian is a version of it.

name: Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope
definition: catadioptric telescope with a corrector plate and a folded mirror light path.

name: Maksutov-Cassegrain telescope
definition: catadioptric telescope with a meniscus corrector and a folded mirror light path.

name: Smart telescope
definition: Telescope with a sensor and no eyepiece that shows the sky on a screen or app.

name: Solar telescope
definition: Telescope made to observe the Sun in hydrogen-alpha light.

name: Spotting scope
definition: compact single-tube telescope for daytime viewing of distant things, used on a tripod or rest.

name: Compound light microscope
definition: microscope with an objective and an eyepiece in series, for thin specimens on a slide.

name: Stereo microscope
definition: low-power microscope with two optical paths giving an upright three-dimensional view of solid objects.

name: Digital microscope
definition: Microscope with its own sensor that shows the image on a screen or computer.

name: Polarizing microscope
definition: microscope that lights the specimen with polarized light, for minerals and crystals.

name: Handheld magnifier
definition: magnifying lens on a handle held in the hand.

name: Folding loupe
definition: small loupe that folds into a case or holder to be carried.

name: Stand magnifier
definition: magnifier on a desk, floor or neck-cord stand.

name: Head-worn magnifier
definition: Loupe or magnifier on a headband or clip; also called a binocular loupe.

name: Eclipse glasses
definition: Glasses with a solar filter made for looking at the Sun.

name: Orrery
definition: Mechanical model of the Sun, planets and moons.

name: Astrolabe
definition: Instrument that models the sky for finding the positions of stars and the time.

name: Planetarium projector
definition: Projector that shows the night sky on a dome or wall.

name: Air thermometer
definition: Instrument that reads the air temperature indoors or outdoors; a working Galileo thermometer counts here.

name: Hygrometer
definition: instrument that reads the humidity of the air.

name: Cistern barometer
definition: mercury barometer whose column stands in an open cistern.

name: Angle barometer
definition: mercury barometer whose tube is bent or sloped to lengthen the scale.

name: Aneroid barometer
definition: barometer that reads pressure from a sealed flexible capsule.

name: Wind vane
definition: instrument that shows the wind direction.

name: Windsock
definition: tapered fabric sleeve that shows wind direction and strength.

name: Rain gauge
definition: instrument that collects and measures rainfall.

name: Pyranometer
definition: instrument that measures solar radiation.

name: Weather station
definition: Set of instruments that measures several weather quantities together, with a display; sensor count and shielding vary by model.

name: Air-quality monitor
definition: Instrument that measures pollutants or particles in the air.

name: Anemometer
definition: instrument that measures wind speed.

name: Beaker
definition: wide cylindrical open vessel with a spout, for holding, mixing and heating liquids.

name: Erlenmeyer flask
definition: conical flask with a narrow neck, for mixing and heating.

name: Volumetric flask
definition: flat-bottomed flask with a long neck and a single mark, for making a solution to an exact volume.

name: Round-bottom flask
definition: round flask for heating and boiling liquids.

name: Test tube
definition: small tube closed at one end, for holding or heating a small sample.

name: Graduated cylinder
definition: tall cylinder with a volume scale, for measuring liquid volume.

name: Pipette
definition: tube for drawing up and delivering a measured amount of liquid.

name: Burette
definition: graduated tube with a tap, for delivering liquid in controlled amounts.

name: Petri dish
definition: shallow lidded dish for culturing cells or microbes.

name: Laboratory balance
definition: balance made to weigh samples in a laboratory.

name: Centrifuge
definition: machine that spins samples to separate their parts.

name: Laboratory incubator
definition: chamber that holds samples at a set warm temperature.

name: Laboratory oven
definition: oven for drying or heating samples at a set temperature.

name: Laboratory freezer
definition: Freezer or ultra-low-temperature unit made for cold storage of samples; laboratory refrigerators are included.

name: Fume hood
definition: Ventilated cabinet that draws fumes from work on samples away from the user.

name: Dissection set
definition: set of instruments for dissecting specimens.

name: Science experiment kit
definition: Kit made to teach science through experiments, sold by subject such as chemistry, physics and electricity, biology, earth and space, or crystals and materials.

name: Telescope eyepiece
definition: eyepiece made for a telescope.

name: Alt-azimuth mount
definition: telescope mount that moves up-down and left-right.

name: Equatorial mount
definition: telescope mount with an axis aligned to the Earth's axis for following the sky.

name: Solar filter
definition: filter made to fit a telescope or binocular for safe viewing of the Sun.

name: Astronomy camera
definition: Camera made only to fit a telescope.

name: Microscope slide
definition: slide made to hold a specimen under a microscope.

name: Microscope camera
definition: Camera or adapter made to fit only one kind of microscope.

name: Pocket microscope
definition: small handheld microscope carried in the pocket.

name: Cassegrain telescope
definition: Telescope whose concave primary and convex secondary mirror fold the light back through a hole in the primary, with no full-aperture corrector plate.

name: Telescope tripod
definition: Tripod made to carry a telescope mount head, sold apart from the mount; a universal photo tripod is in Cameras & Photography.

name: Mount counterweight
definition: Weight fitted on the counterweight shaft of a telescope mount to balance the tube.

name: Tube rings
definition: Pair of rings or a clamp that holds a telescope tube on a mount dovetail.

name: Polar scope
definition: Small sighting scope fitted in an equatorial mount's polar axis to align it on the celestial pole.

name: Equatorial wedge
definition: Tilting plate that sets a fork or alt-az telescope mount at the latitude angle to track equatorially.

name: Eye loupe
definition: Loupe in a short tube held in the eye socket, leaving both hands free; also called watchmaker's loupe.

name: Laboratory condenser
definition: Jacketed glass tube through which coolant flows to turn vapour back into liquid in distillation or reflux.

name: Laboratory autoclave
definition: Pressure chamber that sterilises laboratory ware, media and waste with steam.

name: Laboratory shaker
definition: Device that mixes samples in vessels by orbital, reciprocating or rocking motion.

name: Rotary evaporator
definition: Device that removes solvent from a sample by rotating a flask in a heated bath under reduced pressure.

name: Laminar-flow cabinet
definition: Cabinet that blows HEPA-filtered air over the work surface to keep samples free of contamination.

name: Biosafety cabinet
definition: HEPA-filtered enclosed cabinet that protects the user, the sample and the room when handling biological material.

name: Electron microscope
definition: Microscope that forms an image with a beam of electrons instead of light (scanning or transmission; tabletop models included).

name: Scanning probe microscope
definition: Microscope that maps a surface by scanning it with a fine physical probe (atomic force, scanning tunnelling).

name: Spectrometer
definition: Instrument that splits light from a sample into a spectrum and measures it (UV-Vis, infrared, Raman, emission); a hand spectroscope counts here.

name: Mass spectrometer
definition: Instrument that ionises a sample and sorts the ions by mass to charge to identify its components.

name: Chromatograph
definition: Instrument that separates the components of a sample by passing it through a column (gas or liquid chromatography, HPLC).

name: Elemental analyser
definition: Instrument that measures the elements (carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur and others) a sample contains, usually by combustion.

name: Glove box
definition: Sealed cabinet with fitted gloves for working on samples in an inert or isolated atmosphere.

name: Climatic chamber
definition: Cabinet that holds samples at a set temperature and humidity, below or above room temperature, for stability or ageing tests.

name: Laboratory stirrer
definition: Device that mixes a liquid sample with a stirring bar or paddle, magnetic or overhead, often with a heating plate.

name: Laboratory water bath
definition: Heated tank of water that holds sample vessels at a set temperature.

name: Laboratory circulator
definition: Unit that heats or cools a liquid and pumps it to hold a bath or connected apparatus at a set temperature.

name: Viscometer
definition: Instrument that measures the viscosity of a liquid sample.

name: Rheometer
definition: Instrument that measures how a sample flows and deforms under applied stress or strain.

name: Microplate reader
definition: Instrument that measures absorbance, fluorescence or luminescence of samples in the wells of a microplate.

name: Laboratory thermometer
definition: Thermometer made to read the temperature of a sample, liquid-in-glass or digital probe.

name: Cloud sensor
definition: Instrument that detects cloud cover by measuring the infrared temperature of the sky.

name: Sky-quality meter
definition: Instrument that measures the brightness of the night sky.

name: Microscope stage
definition: Stage made to fit a microscope, manual or motorised, that holds and moves the specimen.

name: Dew shield
definition: Tube fitted to the front of a telescope to keep dew and stray light off the objective.

name: Telescope focuser
definition: Draw-tube unit fitted to a telescope that moves the eyepiece or camera to focus (Crayford, rack and pinion, motorised).

name: Molecular model kit
definition: Set of atom and bond pieces for building models of molecules, made to teach chemistry.

name: Schmidt astrograph
definition: Catadioptric imaging telescope with a full-aperture Schmidt corrector and a spherical primary that forms the image on a camera at prime focus inside the tube, with no eyepiece position.

name: Telescope finder
definition: Small sighting device fitted on a telescope tube to aim it: finderscope, right-angle finder, red-dot or ring sight. The polar scope is listed separately.

name: Barlow lens
definition: Negative lens unit fitted in a telescope's eyepiece barrel that multiplies the effective focal length, and so the magnification, by a stated factor.

name: Astronomical filter
definition: Filter for a telescope eyepiece barrel, filter wheel or camera that passes chosen wavelengths (colour, moon, light-pollution, nebula, narrowband); solar filters are listed separately.

name: Microscope objective
definition: Objective lens that screws into a microscope nosepiece (RMS or M25 thread), sold apart from the stand; class and tube-length standard vary.

name: Microscope eyepiece
definition: Eyepiece made for a microscope tube (23.2 or 30 mm and other barrels), sold apart from the stand; wide-field type and power vary.

name: Focus motor
definition: motor unit fitted to the knob shaft of an existing telescope focuser and driven from a computer or hand box to focus.
